question: Should byte-triggered compaction retries use persisted per-session hysteresis of `max(1 MiB, 10%)` growth, resetting when the active transcript file or configured threshold changes?
rationale: The implementation is technically sound, but the growth window determines how long an oversized transcript may remain above an operator-selected threshold and therefore needs an owner policy decision.

options.title: Accept the hysteresis
options.body: Adopt the branch's additive session metadata and fixed growth window to prevent every-turn byte-compaction loops.

options.title: Tune before merge
options.body: Choose different absolute or relative growth thresholds and update the focused tests before landing.

options.title: Pause for broader policy
options.body: Hold this PR if byte-triggered and token-triggered compaction semantics should be redesigned together.

recommendation.title: Accept the hysteresis
recommendation.body: Adopt the branch's additive session metadata and fixed growth window to prevent every-turn byte-compaction loops.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent merged work owns the closest preflight-compaction gate behavior in current history.
